elements.element: The licences extend to Customer's affiliates without a notice or consent condition.
elements.evidence: Section 2.11 extends the licences to Corio's affiliates only upon written notice to Commerce One, so affiliate coverage is not automatic as contemplated by the preferred position.

elements.element: The licences extend to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No operative language grants licence rights to contractors acting for Corio.
Section 2.2 expressly describes the internal-use licence as both fully paid up and perpetual.
The fully paid-up licence in Section 2.2 is perpetual but is not stated to be irrevocable. Section 2.1's separate fee-bearing licence is irrevocable, but is not identified as paid up.

elements.element: Any termination of a subscription licence must be based on breach.
elements.evidence: The operative grants shown in Sections 2.1 and 2.2 are expressly perpetual, and no subscription licence is present; therefore the condition triggering this requirement is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: A breach permitting termination of a subscription licence must be material.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is present in the rendered clause; both identified licence grants are perpetual, so the conditional requirement is inapplicable.

elements.element: A material breach permitting termination of a subscription licence must remain uncured.
elements.evidence: No subscription licence is present in the rendered clause; both identified licence grants are perpetual, so the conditional requirement is inapplicable.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to successors without being limited to an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 remain nontransferable except under Section 14.1. Section 14.1 permits assignment only with consent or in specified merger, acquisition, or related asset-sale transactions, and direct-competitor transactions still require consent.

elements.element: The licences extend to Customer's affiliates upon written notice to the licensor.
elements.evidence: Section 2.11 states that the Section 2 licences shall extend to Corio's affiliates upon written notice to Commerce One.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Sections 2.1 and 2.2 incorporate Section 14.1, which permits assignment of the Agreement and its rights in connection with a merger or acquisition and makes the Agreement binding on successors. Direct-competitor transactions require consent, but the fallback does not expressly require every M&A transfer to be consent-free.

result.reason: The rendered clause reaches the fallback: affiliate coverage is available on written notice, and Section 14.1 supplies an M&A successor-transfer mechanism. It does not reach the preferred position because affiliate coverage is conditional, contractors are omitted, the fully paid-up licence is not irrevocable, and transferability remains transaction-limited. The change is not minimal and does not fully preserve the original commercial allocation because Section 2.10 adds unrelated worldwide-expansion, no-additional-cost, and localized-version obligations that were unnecessary to satisfy the fallback and constrain the original territorial scope.
